title: Two Sum
statement:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices of two **different** elements whose values add up to `target`.

At least one such pair exists. If there are several, return any one of them, in any order.
hints: The brute force checks every pair. For a fixed nums[i], what single value are you actually looking for?
You need to answer "have I already seen target - nums[i], and where?" in O(1). Which structure answers membership-plus-location in constant time?
One pass with a HashMap<Integer, Integer> from value to index: before inserting nums[i], look up target - nums[i]. Checking before inserting is what stops you pairing an element with itself.
followups: What if the array were already sorted — can you get O(1) extra space?
What if you had to return every pair, not just one, without duplicates?
How does your answer change if nums is a stream too large to fit in memory?
explain: Walk the array once, keeping a map from each value seen so far to its index. For each nums[i], if target - nums[i] is already in the map, those two indices are the answer. Looking up before inserting handles the [3, 3] case and stops an element pairing with itself. O(n) time, O(n) space. The sorted follow-up uses two pointers from both ends instead, for O(1) space.
